stories.headline: DeepSeek Suffers 7+ Hour Outage, Longest Since Its Viral Debut in Early 2025

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek's chatbot suffered a major outage of more than seven hours overnight in China on March 29-30, its biggest since its viral debut in early 2025.
Users reported 'server busy' errors on both the web app and mobile app, with conversations interrupted and content lost. '#DeepSeek崩了' trended on Weibo.
Some Chinese media reported the service disruption lasted up to 12 hours, with issues persisting into March 30 morning.
DeepSeek deployed several updates to rectify the issue; the company said it was investigating the cause of the outage.
Users reflected on their dependence on the tool: 'Only after DeepSeek went down did I realise I no longer knew how to work without it,' one user posted.

stories.headline: Eli Lilly and Insilico Medicine Sign $2.75B AI Drug Discovery Deal With $115M Upfront

key_facts.fact: Eli Lilly signed a deal worth up to $2.75 billion with Hong Kong-listed AI drug developer Insilico Medicine, including $115 million in upfront payments.
Insilico CEO Alex Zhavoronkov said the company has developed at least 28 drugs using generative AI, with nearly half already in clinical trials.
Additional payments beyond the $115M upfront are tied to regulatory approvals, commercial achievements, and licensing fees.
Insilico develops its AI models in Canada and the Middle East, and conducts early-stage drug development in China. The companies have collaborated since 2023.
Andrew Adams from Lilly described Insilico's research as 'a powerful complement' to the company's clinical development capabilities.
Lilly is simultaneously engaged with a DeepMind subsidiary on similar AI drug development projects, signaling a broader commitment to AI in pharma.

stories.headline: Mistral Raises $830M in Debut Debt Financing for Paris-Area AI Data Center

key_facts.fact: French AI startup Mistral raised $830 million in its first-ever debt financing, backed by seven banks including BNP Paribas, Crédit Agricole CIB, HSBC, and MUFG.
The funds will be used to purchase 13,800 Nvidia chips and build a data center in Bruyères-le-Châtel near Paris, expected to become operational in Q2 2026.
The debt financing is the first major deal of its kind to fund European AI infrastructure, reflecting Mistral's push for 'sovereign AI' in Europe.
The transaction reflects growing investor confidence in European AI companies challenging U.S. tech dominance in AI infrastructure.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches Codex Plugins With 20+ Integrations as Sora Compute Shifts to Coding

key_facts.fact: OpenAI launched Codex Plugins on March 29, packaging skills, app connectors, and resource configurations into shareable bundles that expand Codex beyond code generation into workflow automation.
Over 20 plugins are available at launch, including integrations with Figma, Notion, Gmail, Google Drive, and Slack across the Codex app, CLI, and VS Code extension.
Codex has over 2 million monthly active users and is priced at $200/month. OpenAI is redirecting freed GPU compute from the shuttered Sora video tool to Codex.
Codex may be merged with ChatGPT and Atlas into a unified 'super app' as OpenAI focuses resources on coding and reasoning after discontinuing Sora.
A Plugin Directory is planned but not yet fully accessible; OpenAI has not announced a timeline for external plugin submissions.

stories.headline: Pro-AI PAC Innovation Council Action Plans $100M+ Spending in 2026 US Midterms

key_facts.fact: Innovation Council Action, a new pro-AI political group, plans to spend over $100 million in the 2026 U.S. midterm elections to support candidates favoring AI deregulation.
The group is led by Taylor Budowich, a former Trump aide who previously ran the MAGA Inc. super PAC, and is championed by tech investor David Sacks, Trump's White House AI advisor.
Budowich stated: 'President Trump has made it clear, America will win the AI race against China, period...this organization exists to make sure he doesn't fight that battle alone.'
The group has developed a scorecard ranking lawmakers based on their alignment with Trump's AI priorities, which will guide spending decisions.
Other pro-AI groups include Leading the Future ($50M raised from Marc Andreessen and Joe Lonsdale) and a Meta-backed super PAC expecting to spend ~$65 million on state-level races.

stories.headline: Flood of AI 'Vibe-Coded' Apps Overwhelms Apple App Store Review, Stretching Waits to Weeks

key_facts.fact: iOS developers report App Store review times have stretched from under a day to 3+ days, with some updates stuck for over a week, as AI-generated app submissions surge.

The delays are attributed to 'vibe coding' — AI development tools like Claude Opus 4.5 that enable non-developers to generate functional apps from text prompts, flooding the App Store with submissions.
Developer Nikita Bier noted: 'It is now taking longer to get our app approved than it is to build the actual features.'
The App Store has seen an influx of new apps each month since 2025, with submissions increasing faster than Apple's review capacity.

stories.headline: Bluesky Launches Attie, an AI Agent App Using Claude to Build Custom Social Feeds

key_facts.fact: Bluesky launched Attie, described as the first agentic social app on AT Protocol, enabling users to design their own feed algorithms and 'vibe-code' custom applications using AI.
Attie is powered by Anthropic's Claude model and was presented at the Atmosphere conference by former CEO Jay Graber (now chief innovation officer) and CTO Paul Frazee.
The app is currently in invite-only closed beta, with conference attendees at the Atmosphere event serving as initial beta testers.
Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider described Attie as making the open AT Protocol accessible to non-engineers who want to customize their social experience.

stories.headline: DeepSeek Suffers 12-Hour Outage Affecting 355M+ Users, Longest Downtime Since Debut

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek's chatbot went offline Sunday evening (March 29) and was not fully restored until Monday morning (March 30), totaling approximately 12 hours of downtime
DeepSeek had over 355 million users as of February, making this outage one of the largest AI service disruptions to date
Chinese social media was flooded with complaints, with one user saying: 'Only after DeepSeek went down did I realise I no longer knew how to work without it'
Local rivals including Zhipu AI, MiniMax AI, and Moonshot AI have made major performance gains with their own releases, outshining DeepSeek
This was DeepSeek's second major disruption; the platform suffered denial-of-service attacks in late January following its R1 model release

stories.headline: Samsung Semiconductor Workers Announce 18-Day Strike From May 21, Threatening Chip Supply

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics' labor union plans an 18-day general strike starting May 21, 2026, with a union rally scheduled for April 23
Around 70% of the union's members are from Samsung's Semiconductor Division (DS), making it the primary target of the action
The union estimates potential company damages between 5 trillion and 10 trillion Korean won if the strike occurs
DDIC and PMIC supply would be affected first, with prices expected to rise and disruptions potentially extending into Q3 2026
The core dispute is over removal of the performance bonus (OPI) cap, currently limited to 50% of annual salary

stories.headline: Mistral Raises $830M Debt to Build 13,800-GPU Nvidia-Powered Data Center Near Paris

key_facts.fact: Mistral AI secured $830 million in debt financing from seven global banks: HSBC, BNP Paribas, Crédit Agricole CIB, La Banque Postale, MUFG, Natixis CIB, and Bpifrance
The data center at Bruyères-le-Châtel near Paris will house 13,800 Nvidia GB300 GPUs with 44 MW initial capacity, expected operational in Q2 2026
Mistral aims to scale to 200 MW across Europe by end of 2027, with a parallel €1.2 billion expansion initiative in Sweden announced in February
This is Mistral's debut debt financing and the first major such deal to fund European AI infrastructure; the company has raised approximately $2.9 billion overall
Mistral is pursuing sovereign AI infrastructure independent of US cloud providers, with total planned infrastructure spend of €4 billion

stories.headline: Amazon Acquires Fauna Robotics, Maker of $50K Humanoid Robot Sprout

key_facts.fact: Amazon acquired New York-based Fauna Robotics, maker of the 3.5-foot-tall humanoid robot Sprout, which costs $50,000; financial terms of the deal were not disclosed
Sprout can dance (the Twist and Floss), pick up objects like toy blocks or teddy bears, stand up from a chair, and walk; Disney was among its first customers
Fauna Robotics will operate as 'Fauna Robotics, an Amazon company' under CEO Rob Cochran, and is described as a software developer platform sold to academic and corporate research laboratories
Amazon already operates over 1 million robots in its warehouse operations; the acquisition came just under two months after Sprout's introduction in January 2026
Amazon previously attempted to acquire iRobot in 2024 but abandoned the purchase due to regulatory challenges in Europe and the US

stories.headline: China's Agibot Rolls Out 10,000th Humanoid Robot, Hitting Milestone in Just 3 Months

key_facts.fact: Agibot announced the rollout of its 10,000th humanoid robot on March 30, 2026, making it the global leader in humanoid robot shipments
Production accelerated dramatically: first 1,000 units took ~2 years, 1,000 to 5,000 took ~1 year, and 5,000 to 10,000 took just 3 months (4x faster than the previous phase)

Agibot was ranked #1 globally in humanoid robot shipments in 2025 by industry analysts, and is expanding beyond China into Europe, North America, Japan, South Korea, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East
Robots are deployed across logistics, showroom navigation, retail, hospitality, education, and industrial production lines

stories.headline: China Opens First Automated Humanoid Robot Manufacturing Line With 10,000-Unit Annual Capacity

key_facts.fact: China's first fully automated humanoid robot manufacturing line went into operation on March 29, 2026 in Foshan City, Guangdong Province, with annual capacity of 10,000 units
The line produces one humanoid robot every 30 minutes on average, using 24 digitalized precision assembly processes and 77 safety testing procedures
The manufacturing line is over 50% more efficient than traditional methods and supports mixed-model, multi-unit assembly with high flexibility
The facility marks a major step in China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), which identifies humanoid robotics as a strategic sector

stories.headline: Wired Exposé: Waymo and Austin School District Struggled for Months to Train Robotaxis to Stop for School Buses

key_facts.fact: Emails, texts, and NTSB reports obtained by Wired show Waymo and an Austin school district struggled for months to train robotaxis to stop for school buses as required by law
Waymo cars have received at least two dozen school bus violations in Austin, including at least four since a November software update intended to fix the issue
Waymo is now providing 500,000 paid robotaxi rides every week across its operating cities
Waymo's cautious driving results in trips taking up to 30% longer than with human drivers, and a Waymo car blocked an emergency response in a separate Austin incident

stories.headline: VW, Mercedes, Waymo, and Pony.ai Push Robotaxis Into European Cities Despite Regulatory Hurdles

key_facts.fact: Waymo plans to begin driverless rides in London by September 2026, while Verne, Uber, and Pony.ai started on-road testing in Zagreb, Croatia as of March 26
Mercedes-Benz is testing Level 4 S-Class vehicles with partner Momenta, targeting German cities late 2026/early 2027, with plans to remove safety drivers in 2027
VW's Moia division is completing pilot phase with ID Buzz AD in Hamburg and Berlin, with full commercial operation slated for late 2026
By 2030, approximately 120,000 robotaxis could operate across European cities; entering new markets requires two years and roughly $15-30 million per city

stories.headline: SpaceX Launches Transporter-16 Rideshare Mission With 119 Payloads From Vandenberg

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched its Transporter-16 dedicated smallsat rideshare mission on March 30, 2026 at 6:20 a.m. ET from Vandenberg Space Force Base, California
The mission carried 119 payloads to sun-synchronous orbit aboard a Falcon 9 rocket, deploying satellites for multiple customers simultaneously
NASA science and engineering projects were among the payloads, including technology demonstrators for various upcoming missions

stories.headline: Reports: Nvidia to Showcase N1 ARM Laptop SoC at Computex 2026, Challenging Qualcomm

key_facts.fact: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will reportedly showcase the N1 and N1X laptop SoCs at Computex 2026 in June, with substantial booth space booked at the Taipei International Convention Center
The flagship N1X features a 20-core ARM CPU paired with a Blackwell-based integrated GPU, targeting gaming laptops; the standard N1 focuses on mainstream AI-capable laptops
Both chips are derived from a GB10-based consumer SoC developed through a partnership between Nvidia and MediaTek, targeting Qualcomm's Snapdragon X Elite

stories.headline: Chinese Photonic Chipmaker Yuanjie Posts 138% Revenue Surge to $87M Ahead of Hong Kong IPO

key_facts.fact: Yuanjie Semiconductor's 2025 revenue rose 138.5% to 601.4 million yuan (~$87M), with net profit of 191 million yuan versus a 6.1 million yuan loss in 2024
Data center revenue surpassed telecoms for the first time, generating 393.3 million yuan (65.4% of total revenue) — a 719% year-over-year increase
Yuanjie is ranked sixth globally among laser chip providers and is the second-largest supplier of laser chips for silicon photonics-based high-speed optical interconnects
The company's stock hit 1,100 yuan/share on the Shanghai STAR Market, giving it a market cap of ~94.6 billion yuan ($13.7 billion); it is pursuing a dual A+H listing in Hong Kong

stories.headline: WTO MC14 Talks Deadlock on Digital Tariff Moratorium Amid US-India Clash

key_facts.fact: WTO ministerial talks in Yaoundé, Cameroon stretched into overtime on March 29 with no agreement on extending the decades-old e-commerce tariff moratorium set to expire in March 2026.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer advocated for a permanent ban on e-commerce tariffs, while India proposed only a two-year renewal.
Western delegates suggested a decade-long compromise as middle ground, but broader consensus for anything beyond 24 months remained elusive.
Beyond e-commerce, delegates wrestled with transparency around government subsidies and modernizing the WTO's consensus-driven decision-making.

stories.headline: UAE Intercepts 16 Iranian Ballistic Missiles and 42 Drones; 11 Killed, 178 Injured

key_facts.fact: UAE air defenses intercepted 16 ballistic missiles and 42 drones launched by Iran on Sunday, March 29, 2026.
The attack killed 11 people — 2 UAE Armed Forces members, 1 Moroccan civilian contractor, and 8 foreign nationals from Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh, Palestine, and India — and injured 178.
Since the conflict began on February 28, the UAE has engaged a cumulative 414 ballistic missiles, 15 cruise missiles, and 1,914 drones from Iran.
The UAE Ministry of Defence stated it remains 'fully prepared and ready to deal with any threats' and will 'firmly confront anything that aims to undermine the security of the country.'

stories.headline: Iran Demands Hormuz Recognition and Reparations as Islamabad Mediation Opens

key_facts.fact: Foreign ministers from Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt met in Islamabad on March 29-30 to prepare ground for de-escalation between the US and Iran.
Iran demands an end to hostilities, reparations for damages, guarantees against future attacks, and recognition of its strategic leverage in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iranian President Pezeshkian told Pakistani PM Sharif in a 90-minute call that confidence-building measures are required before Iran considers direct dialogue, noting Iran was 'twice attacked during earlier nuclear talks.'

A potential meeting between US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Iran's FM Abbas Araghchi could happen within days, possibly in Pakistan, but would require Washington to announce at least a temporary pause in strikes.
The meeting was originally scheduled for Ankara but moved to Islamabad due to Pakistan's deepening role in relaying messages between Washington and Tehran.

stories.headline: Merck's WINREVAIR Hits Primary Endpoint in Phase 2 Heart Failure Trial

key_facts.fact: The Phase 2 CADENCE trial of WINREVAIR (sotatercept) met its primary endpoint in patients with combined post- and precapillary pulmonary hypertension and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (CpcPH-HFpEF).
The 0.3 mg/kg dose achieved a 1.02 Wood units PVR reduction (p=0.004) and the 0.7 mg/kg dose achieved 0.75 Wood units reduction (p=0.024), both statistically significant versus placebo.
The trial enrolled 164 patients (median age 75, 69.5% female) with no currently approved treatments for the condition.
Results support advancement to Phase 3 registrational studies, with the 0.3 mg/kg dose potentially optimizing the benefit-risk profile for this population.

stories.headline: Study Finds $143M in Suspicious Profits on Polymarket Over Two Years

key_facts.fact: A study found approximately $143 million in suspicious profits on Polymarket over two years, using patterns consistent with the use of nonpublic information.
Concentrated trades on Polymarket surged minutes before Trump administration policy moves, signaling a systemic market anomaly.
The findings come as prediction markets boom, with Polymarket processing billions in wagers on geopolitical events including the Iran conflict.
Polymarket has begun tightening its rules in response, as whale wallets' edge and regulatory lags create trading windows for informed bettors.

stories.headline: Brent Crude Tops $115 as Gulf Conflict Drives Fed Rate Hike Odds Past 50%

key_facts.fact: Brent crude rose above $115 per barrel, its highest level since July 2022, driven by the ongoing Iran conflict and threats to Strait of Hormuz shipping.
WTI crude futures closed at $99.64, a 40% surge since late February when the Iran-UAE conflict began.
Market probability of a Fed rate hike in 2026 crossed the 50% threshold, effectively eliminating expectations of any rate cuts this year.
The Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.50%-3.75%, with Chair Powell stating 'it is too soon to know the scope and duration of the potential effects' of the energy shock.
February PPI jumped 0.7% exceeding expectations, and gasoline prices are potentially approaching $5/gallon as economists warn inflation could hit 6.4% by June.

stories.headline: Pro-AI Group Plans $100M+ Midterm Spend to Advance Trump Deregulation Agenda

key_facts.fact: Innovation Council Action, a new pro-AI political nonprofit led by former Trump deputy chief of staff Taylor Budowich, plans to spend more than $100 million on the 2026 midterms.
The group is endorsed by David Sacks, the outgoing White House AI czar, and will use a congressional scorecard to reward deregulation supporters and punish critics.
Total AI-industry election spending now exceeds $300 million, with pro-deregulation groups outspending regulators 3-to-1. AI-backed candidates have won 10 of 11 congressional primaries so far.
The $100M+ planned spend would set a record, exceeding Club for Growth Action's $69 million single-PAC midterm record from 2022, though polling shows bipartisan voter skepticism of AI.

stories.headline: India Approves NDC 3.0 Climate Targets: 47% Emissions Intensity Cut by 2035

key_facts.fact: India's Union Cabinet approved NDC 3.0 for the 2031-2035 period, committing to a 47% reduction in emissions intensity by 2035 from 2005 baseline.
India targets 60% of cumulative installed electric power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2035, up from over 52% already achieved by early 2026.
The plan includes creating an additional 3.5-4.0 billion tonnes CO2 equivalent of carbon sinks through forest and tree cover by 2035.
India maintains its long-term target of net-zero emissions by 2070 and has largely met ahead of schedule earlier climate commitments including 36% emissions intensity reduction between 2005-2020.
